why: The statement asks only whether an odd perfect number exists. Unconditional nonexistence claims are scope whole but each is a self-published or unreviewed claim on a landmark problem, with no expert uptake, and later specialist work (Ochem–Zelinsky, Mantovanelli, July 2026) still treats the question as open. Several also carry their own signals: Shiraishi's scope ballooned and he conceded an earlier error, Reed's Lean files do not encode σ(N)=2N, and Liu's premise is incoherent. So all of these are not_credible. Results that settle nonexistence for a class of N are case: smallest prime factor in {5,…,17} (Mantovanelli), the form 13⁵m² (Shiraishi), and few distinct prime factors (Nielsen). Mantovanelli is credible-but-unreviewed: the only objections come from an AI referee. Necessary conditions that hold inside a class without excluding it are none (Yamada, Zelinsky, Stone, Ochem–Zelinsky). That means divisibility, reciprocal-sum bounds and smallest-prime bounds stated in terms of ω. So are conditional proofs (Vega 2022, Figshare, Rodgers) and unread or framework items (Mayo, Bërdëllima). Size lower bounds on N are finite checks, so instances. Tóth is about multiperfect/spoof numbers, so variant. Mantovanelli's acknowledgement (known only from a snippet) describes ChatGPT 5.5 doing formatting, search, presentation and coding support. Nothing places it in the mathematics, so ai_role is none. Vega 2024 has a year-only 2024 date, so after_snapshot is null.
doubts: Mantovanelli's AI disclosure is from an unverified snippet; 'coding support' for the verifier scripts that the closures rest on could, if substantive, merit 'assisted' — the record does not establish that. Treating Nielsen's ω lower bounds as 'case' versus 'none' is a judgement call (pre-snapshot, so it does not affect status). Bërdëllima may contain restricted-form nonexistence cases, but the record does not establish them.
